decontamination_notes: cii-v2 candidate #3 under the hard-band gate (best model <=2/3). zod #6412 'align record keys and intersection strictness with TypeScript' (merged 2026-08-14), which SUPERSEDES THREE prior human attempts (#5905, #6234, #6248) and fixes four issues reported independently over three years (#2200, #2573, #4017, #5663) — strong evidence the correct semantics are easy to get subtly wrong. The convention being implemented is TypeScript's index-signature treatment, which cannot be re-derived from first principles: inside an intersection a record's key schema governs only the keys it matches, a matching key with a wrong value is a value error not a key error, and an operand's refinements still run when the input carries keys that operand alone would reject. Built by differential probing: 28 corners executed at base and gold in the task image; exactly 6 diverge (regex- and template-literal-keyed records in intersections in both directions, plus strict-operand refinements running with extra keys present) and form the 4 fail_to_pass tests; the stable corners are pinned across 6 guards (standalone record excess-key checks, enum/literal exhaustiveness — enum-keyed records stay exhaustive even inside intersections, verified base==gold both directions — strict-object failure on unrecognized keys, intersection reconciliation incl. defaults, pipe semantics, plain object/loose/record basics). Base is the direct parent of the squash merge; gold is the PR's single source file (core/schemas.ts), tests excluded. Assertions use parse results and STRUCTURED issue codes only (sorted code lists), never message text. Per the v2 charter: no fix-location hints, symptoms-plus-required-behavior issue mirroring the upstream reports.
